newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania market regulator okeys new registry.
newsitem.headline: Romania market regulator okeys new registry.

text.p: Romanian capital market regulator CNVM said on Tuesday it had approved the creation of a second shareholders' registry to serve Romania's budding over-the-counter (OTC) market.
"We have authorised the setting up of an independent registry, which will list stockholders in the southern regions of Muntenia and Oltenia," CNVM vice-president Mihai Radu said.

He said the registry, which had 10 territorial computing centres as its shareholders, was intended for the OTC market the RASDAQ launched last October to trade around 5,000 companies privatised under a 1995 mass selloff.
The RASDAQ now operates with only one registry -- the Romanian Shareholders' Registry (RRA) -- which so far has signed contracts with 160 of the over 2,300 companies listed in RASDAQ trading.
The Bucharest bourse, which opened late in 1995 and trades 22 stocks, has its own registry.

"A registry other than the RRA will be beneficial for the OTC market, as it will stimulate competition and will prevent the RRA from holding a monopoly," Radu said. "Anyway, more than one registry are needed to handle 5,000 companies."
RRA general manager Mircea Ilie said a new registry would be good for competition but said it would raise brokers' costs.
"Brokerage houses will have to connect to the new registry and this will raise costs, reflecting on spending by clients," he said.
